answer: Cross-epoch behaviour fingerprint matching. Each identity’s action mix is hashed into an atlas of stable role features per epoch; continuity across epochs is required to retain standing. A river of state transitions links epochs, so a clone cluster must replay consistent histories, and any divergence in the saffron-tagged role vector triggers revocation. Attackers pay the full compute and storage cost of maintaining N coherent histories, plus the opportunity cost of lost standing on any mismatch.
